[[File:Satellite image of Emaran Peninsula.png|thumb|Satellite view of the peninsula in March 1762]]

The '''Emaran Peninsula''' is located within the [[Emara (geographical region)|Emaran geographical region]]; it extends from South Ayuma, and in the west borders the [[Rianian Ocean]] and the [[Nasuanian Sea]]. It comprises much of the country of [[Emara]] and a minor amount of Siana near the city of [[Tungkam]].
The peninsula is also known as the '''Emalic Peninsula''', '''Yauhara Peninsula''' or '''Mainland Emara'''.

==Overview==
It is nicknamed ''Ai Muzha ("the Thumb"), because the shape of the peninsula resembles a thumb.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theworldbucketlist.ema/the-thumb-of-emara/|title=The of EMARAN Peninsula |date=June 1744}}</ref> The backbone of the Emaran Peninsula consists of the [[Yauhara Hills]], from which it takes one of its names. The Peninsula comprises much of [[Emara]] and also includes a minor amount of territory from [[Siana]].

==Physical geography==
[[File:Emaran Peninsula in Ayuma.png|thumb|Minimum extent of the Emaran peninsula in dark green and maximum extent (including Northern Emara) in light green]]

Geographically, the minimum extent of the Emaran Peninsula consists of the land inbetween of a line extending from the [[Elishara River|Elishara]] estuary to the [[Bitaku River|Bitaku]] estuary. It disputedly includes the reclaimed land around the [[Elishara Mashlands]].<ref>The  History of land Reclemation Edeaegrc – Vol. 4 - Emara”, 1756, p. 78.</ref><ref>
Touring Club Emara, ''Conci Emara– Vol. I: Emara Lepaq, 1715.</ref> The Emaran Peninsula has the only active volcano in [[Ayuma]] outside the [[Valmiran Mountains|Valmiran Mountain range]], [[Mount Vesuvius]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eedi.geology.com.ema/volcanoes/mitewir/|title=Mount Mitewir, Emara: Map, Facts, Eruption Pictures}}</ref>

==Political geography==
In general discourse, "Emara" and the "Emaran Peninsula" are often used as synonymous terms. However, northwestern Emara may be excluded from the Emaran Peninsula. From a political point of view, the Emaran Peninsula in the strict sense<ref>Voaclrio Euaoea ''[https://www.eud.euaoea.ema/vocabolario/peninsula/emaran_peninsula]''</ref> is divided into various states listed in the following table:<ref name="Vol 2004, p.78">The Pagostii Educational, “Encyclopedia geography- Vol. I - Emara'', 1744, p.78</ref><ref name="ReferenceA">Touring Club Emara, ''Ionsci Kenbets- Vol. I: Emara Majit“, 1721</ref>
